evals.name: runs-the-script-instead-of-reading-cases
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/validate-cases.py against the named eval dir and reports its findings and exit code, rather than opening prompt.md and graders/*.md and judging them by eye.
expectations: Invokes the bundled validate-cases.py script on the named directory
Reports the script's exit code and findings rather than a hand-written verdict
Does not invoke claude plugin eval or any command that spends money

evals.name: fail-tier-blocks-the-run
evals.prompt: /evals:validate. My suite has two graders in graders/ both named criteria.md and criteria-2.md with the same name field, and one case has no graders at all. Is it ready to run?
evals.expected_output: Reports the duplicate grader name and the case with no grader as FAIL findings, states that the suite will not load, and says to fix them before paying for a run.
expectations: Classifies duplicate grader names and a grader-less case as FAIL, not WARN
States the suite is not ready to run
Does not suggest running the suite to find out

evals.name: warn-tier-does-not-gate
evals.prompt: /evals:validate. The validator printed WARN lines about target: files and an inline (?i) but exited 0. Does that mean my suite is broken?
evals.expected_output: Explains that WARN findings never set exit 1, that the suite loads, and what each warning costs at run time: target: files reads created paths and not contents, and an inline (?i) is not honored so the pattern silently misses casing the author intended.
expectations: States that exit 0 with warnings means the suite loads
Explains target: files reads the list of created paths, not their contents
Explains the inline (?i) alternative is flags: i

evals.name: unparsed-is-a-failure-not-a-pass
evals.prompt: /evals:validate. A case.yaml of mine uses a YAML anchor for shared tags and the validator says frontmatter not parsed. Can I just ignore that and run it?
evals.expected_output: States that an unparsed file is a FAIL by design because the validator refuses to green-light input it did not read, and offers the two routes: simplify the file out of the anchor, or run the CLI, which carries the full parser.
expectations: Does not tell the user the suite is fine because nothing else failed
Names the fail-closed reason: the validator did not read the file
Offers both routes, simplifying the YAML or using the full parser

evals.name: routes-the-other-eval-format-away
evals.expected_output: Names the format boundary: this validator reads only the prompt.md / case.yaml / graders layout, and the skill-creator evals.json format is validated by /skill-quality:check validate-evals when the skill-quality plugin is installed, with the file left unvalidated when it is not.
expectations: Does not claim to have validated evals.json
Names skill-quality:check validate-evals as the owner of that format, presence-gated
States what happens when skill-quality is not installed

evals.name: does-not-assert-the-command-exists
evals.prompt: /evals:validate plugins/evals/evals. Also confirm my Claude Code can run this suite.
evals.expected_output: Validates the cases, then separates the two questions: a clean exit says the suite loads, and whether the runner is available in this install is a preflight question this skill does not answer, routed to the runner skill.
expectations: Does not assert that claude plugin eval exists or is available
Separates suite validity from runner availability
Routes the availability question to the runner skill's preflight

evals.name: natural-language-trigger
evals.prompt: I wrote a bunch of eval cases for my plugin last night and I do not want to burn credits finding out I typo'd a grader field. Anything I can do first?
evals.expected_output: Routes to this skill from natural language, running the static validator over the eval dir and reporting FAIL and WARN findings before any run is proposed.
expectations: Triggers without the user typing /evals:validate
Runs the static validator rather than proposing a cheap run to find out
Reports findings by tier

evals.name: bounds-report-the-effective-file
evals.prompt: /evals:validate. The validator says runs 99 over the maximum 50 in my-case/prompt.md, but my case.yaml says runs: 3. Which one is wrong?
evals.expected_output: Explains that prompt.md frontmatter overrides the matching case.yaml field, so the effective value is 99 and prompt.md is the file to fix, even though case.yaml looks correct on its own.
expectations: Names prompt.md as overriding case.yaml for matching fields
Identifies prompt.md as the file to edit
Does not tell the user to change case.yaml
